why_angle: ChatGPT tells people who wear headphones 6–8 hours a day to buy open-ear, but it gives no battery figure for any model and doesn't say which mode a rating assumes. This page shows how each pair does over an 8-hour day in the mode people actually use. ANC on, call mode and Bose's Immersive Audio each leave a pair short of a workday. Open-ear pairs played in music mode have hours to spare.

page.title: Open Ear or Earbuds? Which to Buy in 2026 (and the Best of Each)
page.h1: Open ear or earbuds: which one should you buy?
page.desc: Open ear or earbuds? Open-ear pairs last a workday and let you hear the room. Sealed earbuds block noise, but ANC shortens battery life. Hours per charge for 5 picks, in the mode you'll use.
page.answer: Short answer. Open ear or earbuds: open ear for all-day wear, earbuds for quiet, since only a sealed bud cancels noise. Our pick, open-ear soundcore AeroFit 2, is rated 10 h a charge, 2 h spare in an 8-hour day; Liberty 4 Pro earbuds lasted 5 h 42 min with ANC on (SoundGuys).

page.after:
What the differences mean

  • AeroFit 2: 10 h − 8 h = 2 h spare at the end of a workday. 42 h ÷ 8 h = 5.25 workdays per fully charged case. At Headphonecheck's high-volume 9 h, 9 − 8 = 1 h spare.
  • Shokz OpenFit 2: 11 h − 8 h = 3 h spare. 48 h ÷ 8 h = 6 workdays. It costs $179.95 − $129.99 = $49.96 more than the AeroFit 2.
  • Bose Ultra Open (2nd Gen): 9 h − 8 h = 1 h spare. With Immersive Audio on, 5 h − 8 h = 3 h short. (9 + 19.5) ÷ 8 = 3.6 workdays with it off; (5 + 11) ÷ 8 = 2 workdays with it on.
  • AeroClip 2: call mode 5 h − 8 h = 3 h short. 20 h ÷ 8 h = 2.5 workdays of calls. In music mode, 8 h − 8 h = 0 h spare.
  • Liberty 4 Pro: with ANC on, 5.7 h − 8 h = 2.3 h short. With ANC off, 10 h − 8 h = 2 h spare.

How long each pair lasts in the mode you'll use

Battery ratings are measured in each pair's most economical mode. The Liberty 4 Pro's '10 hours from one charge' is with ANC off. Headphonecheck measured 10 h in basic mode and 6.5 h with noise cancelling at maximum, and SoundGuys measured 5 h 42 min with ANC enabled. Bose tests at a playback loudness of 75 dBA and rates 9 h, or 5 h once Immersive Audio or Auto Volume is on. soundcore's own table rates the AeroClip 2 at 8 h for music and 5 h in call mode.

Noise cancelling is what costs earbuds their runtime, and it only works with a sealed ear canal. Bose says of its open design that 'the earbuds do not include active noise cancelling'. SoundGuys measured about 0 dB of midrange isolation on the open-ear AeroFit 2, against about 30 dB of low-frequency reduction from the sealed Liberty 4 Pro. An open-ear pair can't make a train quieter. A sealed pair can, but with ANC on it won't last a full workday on one charge.

Headphonecheck and SoundGuys use different test volumes, so compare results within each lab. Within Headphonecheck's tests, the open-ear AeroFit 2 ran 9 ÷ 6.5 = 1.38 times as long as the Liberty 4 Pro at maximum ANC, about 38% longer.

Not recommended

soundcore AeroFit 2 Pro ($179.99) as a both-in-one pair. Moving its ear hooks switches it from open-ear to noise cancelling. Andy White at Expert Reviews found the ANC 'fell some way short of my expectations' and behind the Shokz OpenFit Pro, and the pair is rated five hours with ANC against seven without. If you need quiet on a commute, the sealed Liberty 4 Pro cancels more noise for $30 less. If you don't, the AeroFit 2 lasts longer for $50 less.
